# Losses of the sum over histories

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> A truncation misses exactly what it drops, possibility cannot see a cancellation, memory must be kept in the configuration, and loops double the courses.

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

For every weighting, the sum over kept and dropped courses is the sum over those kept added to the sum over those dropped (Weights.truncation); where alternatives only add (counting), a truncation bounds the whole from below (counting_truncation_le). Signed counts (signed: pairs of what adds and what subtracts, alternatives adding part by part, a subtracting step turning what follows around) satisfy the laws of weights. With one configuration and two moves back to it, one adding and one subtracting, each course is possible and so is their join, while the signed count of the one step is (1, 1), what adds equalling what subtracts (Interference.cancels); keeping the first course alone gives (1, 0) (Interference.truncation_misses_cancellation); and every reading into possibility that keeps the join of alternatives and marks a course possible marks possible every sum the course enters, balanced or not (Interference.unseen), the balanced join of the two courses among them (Interference.unseen_balanced). A possibility weighting of two-step courses on one configuration requiring the second move to differ from the first is not the weight along courses of any step weight and end reading on that configuration (Memory.not_of_steps), and is one on configurations keeping the last move (Memory.of_kept). With one configuration and two moves back to it, the count of courses of n steps is 2^n (Loop.courses_double). No premise.

Canonical source: [Weighted.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Weighted.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- Signed counts are pairs of natural numbers compared by balance (what adds equalling what subtracts), not integers: the core takes no quotient.
- The theorems on cancellation, memory and loops are witnesses: each is stated on one given small world.

P82 (work board), answering Ren's question of 12 October 2026: “how how accurate can we do that uh what is the limitation do we have losses”. Reading (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation): the limits of accuracy are these four losses, each a theorem: a truncation misses exactly what it drops; possibility cannot see a cancellation (amplitudes cancel, possibility does not); a weighting that depends on how one came must have what it needs kept in the configuration, the loss being in the description, not the unfolding; loops multiply courses without bound, so a sum over every horizon has no finite value without more structure. See the integration document §104.

- Possible courses cancel (Interference.cancels); a weighting depending on how one came is not one of steps (Memory.not_of_steps). [Weighted.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Weighted.lean)
